items.title: Novo Owner to Build $62 Million Quantum Chip Plant in Denmark
items.author: Sanne Wass
items.content: <article>The foundation that controls Ozempic maker Novo Nordisk A/S is building a new quantum chip factory in Copenhagen as the global race to develop the emerging technology heats up.</article>

items.title: India Launches Rocket in Boost to Space Ambitions
items.content: <article>India’s space program notched a much-needed success with a rocket launch on Friday, after two consecutive failures of another launcher that had long served as its workhorse rocket. Bloomberg's Mihir Mishra reports. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Andreessen-Backed AI Startup Gimlet Is Valued at $3 Billion in New Round
items.author: Dina Bass
items.content: The company, which helps divide AI tasks among different chips, raised $300 million in its latest round

items.title: SoftBank Group Prices ¥1 Trillion Retail Bond at 4.75%
items.author: Takahiko Hyuga
items.content: <article>SoftBank Group Corp. priced a ¥1 trillion ($6.3 billion) retail bond with a coupon of 4.75%, as higher rates boost the appeal of bonds, potentially drawing more companies to retail funding.</article>

items.title: Magnetar Founder on AI’s Impact on Investors’ Mindsets
items.content: <article>Alec Litowitz, Founder of Magnetar and now head of his family office, Qstar Capital, discusses his new book, "The Adaptability Quotient," which focuses on decision-making when old strategies stop working. He links the book’s themes to his experience at Magnetar, saying the firm looked for periods of rapid change because uncertainty often drives others away and creates opportunity for those first able to resolve it. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Skylar CIO: AI & Power Story Will Play Out Over Years
items.content: <article>Bill Perkins discusses a new ETF built around short-dated electricity futures in PJM and ERCOT, saying it gives investors direct exposure to power pricing rather than to utilities themselves. He argues the product is timely because electricity demand is expected to grow, driven by manufacturing reshoring, data centers, and the broader AI buildout. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Crusoe Raises Over $3 Billion in Funding at $30 Billion Valuation
items.author: Rebecca Torrence, Dina Bass and Edward Ludlow
items.content: <article>Crusoe, a cloud-computing provider and data center developer doing business with OpenAI, Microsoft Corp. and Meta Platforms Inc., has raised over $3 billion in a funding round that values the startup at roughly $30 billion, according to people familiar with the situation.</article>

items.title: ValueEdge Chair: SpaceX Needs A Succession Plan
items.content: <article>Nell Minow, Chair of ValueEdge Advisors, says Anthropic is moving in the opposite direction from SpaceX on governance, but argues its structure is still unusual and potentially problematic. She says the company is combining elements of public companies and nonprofits, including a public benefit corporation framework that she says both cares about shareholder value and does not. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Apple Headhunter on Ternus Era: Best AI Talent Will Win
items.content: <article>Jeff Christian, who says he oversaw the last two board searches at Apple under Steve Jobs and argues that the selection of John Ternus signals a strategic shift. The discussion then moves to what a hardware engineer can bring to Apple, especially given concerns that the company’s bigger challenges may lie in software and AI rather than hardware. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: David Booth: Shocked People are Anxious About Investing
items.content: <article>David Booth, Co-Founder of Dimensional Fund Advisors, discusses his new book, "Stay Calm," which blends memoir and investment guidance. Booth’s discusses his long-standing message to investors: ignore short-term market noise, avoid trying to outguess the market, and stay invested rather than panic during volatility. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: India Space Surveillance Gets Boost With Successful GSLV Launch
items.author: Mihir Mishra
items.content: <article>India’s space program notched a successful rocket launch on Friday, placing an Earth-observation craft into orbit as New Delhi works to sharpen its satellite-based surveillance capabilities.</article>

items.title: FBI Investigating Possible Exposure of Millions of American IDs
items.author: Patrick Howell O'Neill
items.content: <article>The FBI is investigating a potential breach of an ID verification company that may have exposed scans of millions of Americans’ driver’s licenses, a bureau spokesperson told Bloomberg News on Thursday.</article>

items.title: OpenAI’s Altman Unveils Astra as a New Step Toward AGI | The Close 9/3/2026
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Barings Head ofMulti-Asset Solutions Trevor Slaven, Ciena President & CEO Gary Smith, Skyworks Chair Chris King, S&P Global Global Head of Quantitative Research and Solutions Daniel Sandberg, OpenAI CEO & Co-Founder Sam Altman, UBS Alignment Partners Managing Director, Wealth Management Alli McCartney, SW Retail Advisors President & Founder Stacey Widlitz, Sports Agent Leigh Steinberg, Zumba Fitness CEO & Co-Founder Alberto Perlman, & Daydream Founder & CEO Julie Bornstein. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Daydream CEO on AI’s Impact on Back-To-School Shopping
items.content: <article>Julie Bornstein, Founder & CEO of Daydream, says back-to-school season is becoming a major test case for AI-powered shopping. She explains that Daydream works as an app and website where users can describe themselves and then chat with an AI agent to get personalized shopping results. She speaks with Scarlet Fu & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Skyworks Chair: It Will Be a While Before This Cycle Ends
items.content: <article>Chris King, Chairman of Skyworks Solutions, is introduced as a semiconductor industry veteran with more than 50 years of experience. The segment highlights her time at IBM, her role as the first female CEO of a chip company at AMI Semiconductor, and that company’s later acquisition by Onsemi. She speaks with Scarlet Fu & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Anthropic Executive Doesn’t Want to ‘Buy Market Share’ With Price Cuts
items.author: Shirin Ghaffary
items.content: <article>The Claude maker is competing with more affordable options from rivals</article>

items.title: Los Angeles Schools Ban Student Use of AI Tools on District Devices
items.author: Andrew Oxford and Erin Hudson
items.content: <article>The Los Angeles Unified School District is barring students from using generative AI tools on district devices as part of a broader push to reduce screen time in the classroom.</article>

items.title: Adobe Names Chakravarthy CEO, While Other Contender Departs
items.author: Brody Ford
items.content: <article>Adobe Inc. named Anil Chakravarthy, the leader of its marketing and analytics software business, as its next chief executive officer, thrusting the company veteran into a challenging competition with artificial intelligence upstarts.</article>

items.title: Crusoe Signs Roughly $13 Billion AI Cloud Deal With Jane Street
items.author: Rebecca Torrence and Dina Bass
items.content: <article>Crusoe, a data center upstart with contracts to supply AI computing power to the likes of Meta Platforms Inc. and Oracle Corp., has signed a cloud contract with trading firm Jane Street Group valued at around $13 billion, according to people with knowledge of the matter.</article>

items.title: Chipmaker Longsys Said to Raise $903 Million in HK Listing
items.author: Julia Fioretti and Sangmi Cha
items.content: <article>Shenzhen Longsys Electronics Co. has raised HK$7.08 billion ($903 million) after pricing its Hong Kong listing below the maximum, according to people familiar with the matter.</article>
